material_definitions: The materials investigated are lithium argyrodite superionics with the general formula Li(6+x)P(1-x)Si(x)S5Br.
Ionic conductivity was measured using temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy.
Increasing Si4+ content increases the amount of Li+ and results in increased conductivity at room temperature, reaching a maximum for x = 0.35.
The impedance data was fit using an equivalent circuit consisting of one parallel CPE/resistor in series with a CPE, representing blocking electrodes.
measurements.source_caption: Room temperature conductivity of Li(6+x)P(1-x)Si(x)S5Br as a function of Si4+ content. With increasing Si4+ content, the ionic conductivity increases, leading to the highest conductivity for x = 0.35.

material_definitions: The materials are silicon-substituted lithium thiophosphate argyrodites with the general formula Li6+xP1-xSixS5Br.
Substitution of phosphorus by silicon (x = 0 to 0.5) is used to systematically increase the lithium content.
Ionic conductivity is characterized by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy as a function of temperature.
Arrhenius plots of ln(sigma T) vs 1000/T are used to determine activation energies and conductivities.
measurements.source_caption: Fig. 5 (a) Representative Arrhenius fits of the conductivity values for  $\text{Li}_{6+x}\text{P}_{1-x}\text{Si}_x\text{S}_5\text{Br}$  obtained from impedance spectroscopy and (b) the corresponding impedance responses at room temperature. (c) Representative fit of the composition x=0.175 with the employed equivalent circuit. The data were fit until 1 MHz (red data point), providing a high ideality of the process and capacitances in the range of bulk transport ( $\sim$ 0.134 nF cm $^{-2}$ ). The apex frequency corresponds to 3.8 MHz.

material_definitions: Solid solutions of Li6+xP1-xSixS5Br where Si4+ substitution for P5+ increases the Li+ concentration.
The series is based on the argyrodite crystal structure.
The study investigates how ionic conductivity varies with silicon content x.
measurements.source_caption: Fig. 6 (a) Room temperature conductivity of  $\text{Li}_{6+x}\text{P}_{1-x}\text{Si}_x\text{S}_5\text{Br}$  as a function of  $\text{Si}^{4+}$  content. With increasing  $\text{Si}^{4+}$  content, the ionic conductivity increases, leading to the highest conductivity for x = 0.35. (b) Activation barrier  $E_A$  for ion migration, showing no visible dependence on the Si<sup>4+</sup> content
